why_we_think_it_failed: Nigerian English: 'peanuts burger, can you make peanuts burger' became 'Pinozboga, Kainmek Pinozboga'. Whisper wrote down the sounds it heard as a made-up word. The clip is short (1.9 s) and 'peanuts burger' is an unusual phrase, so the model had no surrounding sentence to help it guess the words. Personal mode got closer ('Pinozburger') but still wrong.

Jamaican English: 'me prefers Naruto more than Dragon Ball Z' became 'I prefer to know what's off with my underground boundary'. Two problems at once: rare names (anime titles) and Jamaican Creole grammar ('me prefers'). Whisper's built-in language model pushes output toward common Standard English phrases, so it replaced unfamiliar words with familiar-sounding ones.
